A spec is one JSON object. Paths are relative to the spec file. Unknown fields produce a warning (`spec-unknown-key`) and are ignored.

text: The file contains death counts but no data date or original source. I’ll map totals with proportional circles. Fourteen rows have no matching geography, including several territories and ship records; I’ll list those omissions with the map.

import json
p='covid-deaths.json'
s=json.load(open(p))
s.update(title='COVID-19 deaths by country',subtitle='Circle area represents reported deaths • Data date not supplied',source='deaths.csv (provided file; original source not supplied)',note='Totals are not adjusted for population. 14 unmatched territory or conveyance rows omitted.',type='symbols',projection='auto',size={'width':1400},symbols={'color':'#b64239','maxRadius':38})
s['data'].update(kind='count',label='Reported deaths')
open(p,'w').write(json.dumps(s,indent=2)+'\\n')
PY

Created the map: [PNG](covid-deaths.png) · [SVG](covid-deaths.svg) · [Interactive HTML](covid-deaths.html).

Circle area represents total deaths, without population adjustment. Matched 226 of 240 rows; no automatic fixes were needed. The file supplies no data date or original source. Seven zero values have no visible circles, and circles overlap in crowded regions.

Omitted rows: Bonaire/Saint Eustatius/Saba, French Guiana, Gibraltar, Martinique, Mayotte, Réunion (encoding damaged), Guadeloupe, Tokelau, five international conveyance records (American Samoa, Solomon Islands, Vanuatu, Diamond Princess, Kiribati), and International commercial vessel.
